# Changing Values Stored in Variables

#### Course: Learn Java Basics

## Changing Values Stored in Variables

Here's how we can update the values stored in variables as needed. Consider the following example:

```java
1class Main {
2    public static void main(String[] args) {
3        
4        int age = 22;
5        System.out.println(age);
6        
7        age = 24;
8        System.out.println(age);
9    }
10}
```

Output

```text
22
24
```

Here,

- The initial value of age is 22. So, the first print statement prints 22.
- The line age = 24; changes the value of age to 24. So, the second print statement prints 24.

![Change value of age from 22 to 24](data:image/png;base64,)

Note that when updating the value of a variable, we do not need to specify its data type again. We simply assign the new value using the assignment operator (=).
